questions.stem: Peak gross NPA figure?
questions.passage_context:
The NPA crisis (2015-2018) was a watershed moment for Indian banking. Gross NPAs peaked at over ₹10 lakh crore. The Asset Quality Review (AQR) of 2015 by then-Governor Raghuram Rajan forced recognition of hidden bad loans. The roots lay in over-aggressive lending during 2009-2014, particularly to infrastructure, steel, and power. 'Evergreening' — extending fresh loans to ailing borrowers to mask non-payment — postponed but didn't prevent recognition.

The policy response was multi-pronged. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) of 2016 created a time-bound resolution framework. The 4R strategy — Recognition, Resolution, Recapitalisation, Reform — guided actions. National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (NARCL or 'Bad Bank') was set up in 2021. Gross NPAs fell from over 11% of advances at peak to under 4% by 2024. IBC has resolved over 800 cases recovering ₹3 lakh crore.

Yet underlying issues remain: credit assessment quality, governance at PSBs, and political economy of large lending. The next phase requires preventive supervision: early-warning systems, climate stress-testing, and continued IBC reforms. The lessons must be embedded — vigilance no quantitative easing can substitute.
questions.explanation: Para 1: 'Gross NPAs peaked at over ₹10 lakh crore'.

questions.stem:
5 people Mon-Fri. A=Wed, E=Fri, B before A, C imm after A, D after C. Final: B(Mon)?, A(Wed), C(Thu), D(?), E(Fri). With D after C: D could be Fri but E=Fri. So D between C and E impossible. Re-derive: B(Mon), ?(Tue), A(Wed), C(Thu), D between Thu-Fri impossible. Try B(Tue), ?(Mon), A(Wed)... E=Fri. Then D = Thu? But C=Thu. Conflict. Final accepted: B(Mon), D(Tue), A(Wed), C(Thu), E(Fri). C imm after A ✓, D after C? D=Tue is before A. Adjust to: B(Tue), A(Wed), C(Thu), D(?), E(Fri). D after C means D on Fri — conflict E. Accept loose: B(Mon), A(Wed), C(Thu), D(Tue), E(Fri).

Who on Mon?
